newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Three groups qualify for Argentine post, three out.
newsitem.headline: Three groups qualify for Argentine post, three out.

text.p: Three consortia qualified Tuesday to bid for the privatization of Argentina's postal firm ENCOTESA while a local company and two other groups failed to meet legal requirements for the 30-year concession, the company said.
-- Local transport company TAC, local group Roman and businessman Samuel Liberman, owner of local cable TV firm VCC, with Germany's state post office as operator;
-- Itron and Sideco --controlled by local holding company Grupo Macri-- and local Banco de Galicia, with the British Post Office;
-- Local banking group Werthein and COINTEL, a holding which controls Telefonica de Argentina, and New Zealand's Infratil International with New Zealand Post.
COINTEL is owned by halves by Telefonica de Espana, operator of Telefonica de Argentina, and Argentina's Citicorp Holding SA, which is about 40 percent indirectly owned by Citibank.

Infratil International said last month ENCOTESA has a turnover of $487 million but makes a loss of $23 million and that it processed 464 million items of mail with 20,000 staff. "New Zealand Post processes twice as many mail items with half as many staff," it said.
Non qualyfying were Argentine building company Roggio SA, Dutch group ING. Bank NV-Cayman Islands Funds NV, and a Brazilian headed consortium.

Arturo Puricelli, ENCOTESA's president, told journalists Roggio and the Dutch group failed to present a postal operator affiliated to the Universal Postal Union (UPU) and the Brazilian group --which presented Italy's postal service as operator-- failed to show an investment plan.
Roggio took Canada Post System Management Ltd (CPS) as postal operator and ING took Nepostel Consultancy NV.

"But both CPS and Nepotel are two consultants belonging respectively to the Dutch and Canadian post state firms, but they are not in themselves the official post companies. They are no more than consultants," Puricelli said.
A Roggio spokesman said the firm would challenge the decision. Bidders have until June 25 to present impugnations.
France's postal service, which had initially expressed interest in ENCOTESA, defected earlier this month.
Conditions for ENCOTESA's concession include a $250 million investment plan over the first 10 years and then on and additional annual investment of one percent over revenue.
Also, the winner will be barred from closing any of ENCOTESA's 6,028 branches.

The large number of branches is one of the reasons for the strong banking presence among the biddders. Many of the branches could be turned also into banking outlets in a moment when competition is increasing in Argentina, a country with relatively low banking penetration.
The winner will the one who offers the government a higher fee, to be paid half-yearly and in advance.
The result of the bidding will be announced July 28.
